title: Real-life haunts: Explore haunted history on these ghost tours & walks in northern Illinois
excerpt: Experience the paranormal and learn the dark histories of these northern Illinois cities and locales.
content:
Halloween season is here, which means it’s the perfect time to explore the spooky side of northern Illinois.

From guided ghost walks through historic downtowns to tours of abandoned buildings with questionable pasts, the region is home to plenty of eerie experiences.

If you’re looking for chilling local legends, haunted history or a fun night out without the gory jump scares, these ghost tours and paranormal adventures are worth adding to your Halloween bucket list.

DuPage County

Naperville & Aurora Ghost Tours

Explore the dark sides of Naperville and Aurora on one of several ghost and paranormal tours.

U.S. Ghost Adventures offers tours of Aurora’s haunted locations and Naperville Nighttime Nightmares Ghost Tours year-round.

The Ghost Tour of Naperville is led by Naperville historian and paranormal investigator Kevin Frantz, who shares chilling stories of ghost encounters throughout the tour. Tours are available on select Fridays, Saturdays and Sundays and cost $20 cash.

Two Brothers Roundhouse Ghost Tours take guests throughout the historic building on a 90-minute lantern-guided tour. The tour includes an opportunity for guests to participate in a paranormal investigation.

Naperville Hauntings Ghost Walks are led by Naperville native and paranormal expert Diane Ladley. The two-hour lantern-lit evening tours take guests through Naperville’s historic district and the many elegant mansions. Ladley shares stories of the city’s haunted history, paranormal encounters and chilling true stories.

DeKalb County

The Egyptian Theatre, long thought to be one of the most haunted buildings in DeKalb County, offers Boo’ze & Spirits Flashlight Tours year-round. Guests will learn about the spooky history of the nearly 100-year-old theatre. Tickets are $40 per person.

The Ellwood After Dark tours explore the historic Ellwood House Museum in DeKalb. The mansion has long been rumored to be haunted with ghost sightings. The tours are held by a docent using only candlelight. Tours are scheduled for Oct. 16-17 and 23-24.

La Salle County

Hegeler Carus Mansion in La Salle will offer “The Mansion is NOT Haunted” tours Oct. 22-24. The tour explores the 19th Century mansion’s customs and superstitions unique to the Gilded Age. This is a 1-hour tour. General admission tickets are $40.

Awesome Ottawa Tours offers their Graveyard Stories tour that explores the “dark side” of the city’s history and takes guests to the burial locations of some of the area’s notorious murderers, as well as the resting places of Civil War soldiers. Tickets are $35.

Starved Rock Lodge offers ghost tours on Friday, Saturday and Sunday nights in October. The tours are led by costumed guides and take guests to local locations known for paranormal activity. The tours last 90 minutes to two hours and are $30 per person. Tours are not recommended for kids 8 and under.

Lake County

American Ghost Walks takes guests on a seven-hour bus tour, stopping at the “Gate” of Libertyville—where legend tells of a long lost girls’ school massacre, a vengeful witch in a Wadsworth cemetery, the ghosts of Cuba Road and much more. Lunch is at a haunted pub. Tickets are $104 for adults.

Ghost Wauk Tours at the Genesee Theatre in Waukegan return in 2026, with tours scheduled for Thursdays Oct. 15 and 29 and on Halloween. The theatre opened in 1927, and claims about ghost sightings and supernatural experiences have haunted it ever since. The tours include special guests. Tickets are expected to sell out, so don’t wait to get yours (some tours are already sold out as of press time).

The Volo Museum in Volo is offering Paranormal Tours. Guests can explore the historic Volo Cemetery, visit an investigation room featuring hologram storytellers and video evidence, and follow a professional guide through locations where paranormal investigators have repeatedly reported unexplained activity on the museum’s new Paranormal Tours. The tours run Saturdays and Sundays through Nov. 1.

McHenry County

Learn about the sordid history of the historic Woodstock Courthouse on a Woodstock Ghost Walk. Guests can learn more about the ghost sightings and paranormal activities in the Courthouse and many other popular spots around town.

Will County

The Old Joliet Prison will have self-guided “Flashlight Tours” Thursdays through Saturdays in October between 6:30 p.m. and 10 p.m. Visitors will receive branded flashlights and will be assisted in their tours by nearly 30illuminated interpretive signage panels, which provide glimpses into the prison’s operations over its long history, through eras of both reform and retribution. The museum’s knowledgeable assistants will be on-site to answer questions and direct patrons through the complex.
